 Judgement

1.The present appeal is filed under Section 374 of Cr.P.C. against the judgment conviction and
sentence dated 17.05.2013 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, District Dhar in Special
Case No.112/2013, whereby, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo 01 year R.I. with default stipulations.

2.As per the prosecution story, on 21.04.2011, father of the prosecutrix has lodged an FIR against the appellant that he has abducted and committed rape upon her under Section 363, 366/366-A,
376 of IPC.

3 . After investigation, the charge-sheet was filed and the learned trial Court after framing the charges against the appellant under Section 363, 366/366-A, 376 of IPC, has only convicted the appellant vide the impugned judgment only under Section 363 of IPC by acquitting from other charges.

The appellant has preferred this appeal on several grounds but during the course of arguments,
learned counsel for the appellant did not press this appeal on merits and not assail the finding part of judgment.
He confines his argument on the point of sentence only and prays that since the appellant has already undergone approximately two months in jail incarceration out of one year of his jail sentence.

It is also submitted that the prosecutrix has already married with the appellant in Sanjay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103607184/
1 the year 2012, they are having two children and at present, the prosecutrix is residing at the house of appellant itself.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, his jail sentence be reduced to the period already undergone.
It is also submitted that the appellant deserves some leniency as the appellant already suffered the ordeal of the trial since 2011.

It is further submitted that this appeal be partly allowed and the sentence awarded to the appellant be reduced to the period already undergone by enhancing the fine amount or the Court may deems fit in the interest of justice.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer.

On the other hand, counsel for the complainant has not opposed the prayer of the appellant and submits that the complainant/prosecutrix has already married with appellant and they are having two children and she has no objection, if the sentence of the appellant is reduced to the period already undergone.
6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the record, the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant appears to be just and proper.
7 . However, the learned trial Court has not committed any error in appreciation of evidence available on record.

Further, it is found that the Court below considered the evidence available on record and correctly found that the case of the prosecution is well supported by the 3 CRA-728-2013 complainant /victim as well as other witnesses.
The Court below has well considered the material available on record, hence, no infirmity is found in the impugned order of conviction passed by the Court below, accordingly, the same is upheld.

8. So far as the sentence of the appellant is concerned, the appellant has suffered the ordeal of criminal case since 2011 and there is no criminal record/antecedents of the appellant, the prosecutrix has already married with the appellant in the year 2012, they are having two children and at present, the prosecutrix is residing at the house of appellant itself, therefore, this Court finds i t expedient to partly allow this appeal by affirming the conviction of the appellant by reducing the sentence to the period already undergone and imposing fine of Rs.2000/-.

9.In view of the aforesaid, this Criminal Appeal is partly allowed and the sentence of the appellant under Sections 363 of IPC is hereby reduced to the period already undergone with imposing the fine of Rs.2000/-.

In case of default of payment of fine amount, the appellant shall undergo 15 days S.I.
10
The appellant is in jail.
After depositing the aforesaid fine amount, he shall be released from the jail.
The amount of fine if already deposited, shall be adjusted.
11. The judgment of learned trial Court regarding disposal of the seized property stands affirmed.
12. A copy of this order be sent to the concerned trial Court for necessary compliance.
Pending application, stands closed.
Certified copy as per rules.
